transcript:
Meeting header: 
Date: 2026-05-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Alex Ramos (Cerulean Head of ML), Priya Singh (Cerulean ML Engineer), Daniel Kwan (Cerulean SRE)

Auto-generated summary: Technical review focused on quantization tradeoffs and benchmarking plan.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining; quick roll call, and then we'll dive into the INT8/FP8/GPTQ runbook.
[00:10] Alex: hi yep alex here, priya and daniel with me. thanks for setting this up.
[00:15] Priya: morning all.
[00:20] Maya: Maya here from Redwood, excited to go through the details.
[00:25] Jordan: great. goal for today is to align on tradeoffs and agree a bench plan to compare GPTQ and AWQ on your models and dataset.

[02:05] Maya: quick context - Cerulean is running a 13B transformer (custom finetune) for multi-step reasoning in product analytics, 95% of traffic is short chat queries but about 5-10% are longer multi-turn prompts. Primary constraints: p50 latency target 120ms, p95 under 350ms, and cost target to reduce token costs by ~4x vs FP16. Also you want private deployment in VPC with KMS.
[02:40] Alex: that's right, we need on-prem-ish behavior, private control plane, and SOC2 style audit. accuracy drop >1.5% on our KPI metric is a blocker.

[05:10] Maya: ok jumping into quantization modes - high level: INT8 (symmetric per-channel or per-tensor), FP8 (bfloat-like, needs hardware support or emulation), GPTQ (post-training quant with group-wise/hessian aware heuristics), AWQ (recent awq-style methods optimized for latency and native quant kernels). each has tradeoffs on accuracy and speed.
[05:40] Priya: can you explain AWQ vs GPTQ in plain terms? we've seen both names in RFCs.
[05:48] Maya: sure - GPTQ tends to do a more precise per-block quantization with reconstruction to minimize local MSE; it's often higher accuracy for aggressive 4-bit/8-bit conversions but slower to run the quantization pass and sometimes has higher memory for dequant tables. AWQ tries to structure quant matrices to map well to int8 kernels, it trades a bit of accuracy for much faster inference kernels and smaller runtime overhead. GPTQ may be better for minimal accuracy loss; AWQ often better for throughput/latency in our runtime.

[08:20] Jordan: important note on KV cache - in quantized runtimes we see two pain points: 1) KV cache storage layout and dequant overhead (especially for per-channel schemes), 2) accumulation precision when attention uses quantized keys/values then compute in int32/float32 - can introduce tiny drift over long histories. For your multi-turn sessions we should test 64-512 token histories.
[09:00] Daniel: drift is a big concern; we've had in prod where 400-token histories degrade relevance on 2-step reasoning. what's the mitigation?
[09:10] Maya: options: keep KV in FP16 even if model weights are int8, or use mixed-precision KV buffers; another is periodic re-normalization or short-term cache TTLs. The trade is memory use vs variable latency when rehydrating cache.

[12:30] Priya: what about calibration and accuracy regressions - we see ~1.2% drop on MRR in a quick GPTQ run previously. is that typical?
[12:45] Maya: yes in that ballpark for aggressive 8->4/INT8 conversions on certain layers. We usually try: 1) per-channel quant for linear layers, 2) layerwise outlier handling (clipping), 3) small calibration set (1-5k samples) targeted to your workload. Also sometimes small continued fine-tune (LoRA or delta) on quantized weights reduces regressions.
[13:30] Alex: fine-tune on quantized weights - is that supported in Redwood private? will that break versioning?
[13:40] Jordan: you can run a quant-aware fine-tune workflow in your environment; Redwood supports pinning model versions and rollouts. If you want we can run a canary dedicated pool with quantized model variant.
[14:00] Alex: good.

[16:10] Maya: hardware support note - FP8 requires either hardware support (recent GPUs) or software emulation; FP8 emulation often hurts latency and complexity. INT8 is widely supported by our optimized kernels. For your Dedicated or Private VPC deployment we recommend INT8/AWQ path unless FP8 hardware is explicitly available.
[17:05] Priya: does INT8 always reduce cost 4x? or is that optimistic?
[17:15] Maya: depends - raw memory can be ~2x smaller vs FP16 for weights (16->8 bits), but runtime throughput gains depend on kernel efficiency, batch sizes, KV overhead (if KVs stay at FP16), and whether the GEMM path is the bottleneck. We typically see 1.5-3x cost improvements in real workloads; 4x is possible in ideal throughput-bound scenarios with large batching and full quantization including KV.

[20:30] Jordan: let's talk latency/batching tradeoff - your p50 120ms target for single-turn queries suggests small batches (1-4). Small batches reduce batching efficiency. AWQ's low-overhead kernels help more in this regime. We should characterize tokens/sec at batch sizes 1,2,4,8 and see break-even cost.

[22:50] Daniel: network / VPC notes - if KV kept at FP16 and we host in VPC, memory needs and egress for checkpoint differ; also KMS calls for key retrieval add small latency on cold starts. Any recommendations?
[23:15] Maya: pre-warm the service, cache KMS tokens, and use local HSM if you need <10ms cold start. Redwood Private supports KMS integrations and you can provision HSM-backed keys; we'll document the best practices.

[26:00] Priya: benchmarking specifics - what metrics do we collect?
[26:10] Maya: p50/p95 latency for end-to-end requests, tokens/sec (throughput), CPU/GPU utilization, memory footprint (model + KV), and task accuracy (your internal KPI: MRR/Success Rate). Also per-token cost estimate. We'll provide a spreadsheet template.

[30:40] Jordan: bench plan proposed: run baseline FP16 on a 1k sample validation set (Priya), then run GPTQ quant (Maya) and AWQ quant (Maya) with same calibration set. Measure deltas on accuracy and latency at batch sizes 1/2/4. Also run KV cache long-history test (64/256/512 tokens) to check drift.

[33:15] Priya: how long do GPTQ/AWQ passes take? we have limited CI windows.
[33:25] Maya: GPTQ pass on 13B is typically a few hours on a single GPU (depends on config); AWQ can be faster in some implementations, maybe 1-2 hours. We'll provide estimated runtimes in the sheet.

[36:00] Alex: any obvious red flags? layers that usually break with int8?
[36:10] Maya: attention output projections and layernorm-adjacent matrices are sensitive; sometimes first and last layers benefit from higher precision. Activation outliers (rare large values) also matter - we use clipping heuristics.

[40:30] Daniel: ops-wise in Redwood runtime, is dequant done inline or as fused kernels?
[40:40] Maya: we have fused dequant + GEMM kernels for the common quant formats (int8 with per-channel scale). That reduces extra memory passes. AWQ path uses specialized kernels that minimize dequant overhead which is why it performs well for low-batch requests.

[45:00] Priya: can we get a quick sanity example - expected p95 on our 13B with batch 1?
[45:10] Maya: rough estimate: FP16 p95 ~300-350ms (depends on prompt length). INT8/AWQ optimized might hit 220-280ms p95; GPTQ might be slightly slower or similar depending on kernel mapping. These are rough; bench required.

[47:50] Alex: about accuracy regression thresholds - we have internal SLA that >1.5% drop on key metric needs exec signoff. Are there rollback strategies?
[48:00] Jordan: yes - Redwood supports canary rollouts and auto-fallback policies. You can deploy quant variant to X% of traffic and fallback to FP16 on quality alerts. Also traffic routing by model tag is supported.

[51:15] Priya: any gotchas for on-prem deployment with quantized models? filesystem permissions for mmap'd checkpoints?
[51:25] Maya: ensure GPU compute drivers and libcudnn/cuBLAS versions match; memory-mapped read-only weights are common; ensure kernel modules allow large page mapping. We'll put a preflight checklist in the doc.

[54:00] Jordan: ok let's recap next steps - Maya will share config sheet & prior benchmarks; Priya will prepare validation subset and run FP16 baseline; Maya+Priya to run GPTQ and AWQ and post results; Daniel to spin up VPC test environment for smoke test; Jordan to follow up on pricing and pilot.

[55:15] Alex: sounds good. one more question - do you have any recommended calibration set size?
[55:25] Maya: 1k-5k examples representative of your production prompts; we often start with 1k to iterate quickly then expand if delta is high.

[56:10] Priya: we'll start with 1k.
[56:20] Jordan: cool. I'll log the action items. thanks everyone.
[56:40] Maya: thanks, we'll upload the sheet now - link: (shared doc) https://redwood.app/sheets/quant-bench-cerulean (note: placeholder link)
[56:55] Daniel: thanks.
[57:10] Alex: appreciate it. bye.

End transcript.
